title: I got tired of wondering whether my AI GM was fudging dice, so I made it impossible
author: Fearless_Math_8561
selftext:
I make a play-by-post RPG where an LLM runs the table as game master. The hardest design problem wasn’t the narration — it was trust: the same model that writes the story also reports the dice, so “the goblin crits you” is unfalsifiable. Players feel this fast, and “trust me” is worth nothing.

Our fix is deliberately boring — commit-reveal (Blum, 1981), applied to a generative narrator:

	**•**	Before the model reads a single player action, the server pre-rolls every die the round could need and stamps a SHA-256 of the manifest onto the round. Player d20s ride as salted per-player commitments, so the seal publishes even when a roll stays hidden for drama.

	**•**	The model never rolls anything. It’s handed the dice and writes the scene around them. A deterministic rules engine recomputes every outcome from the sealed dice — the model’s narration can’t inflate damage, flip a miss, or invent a hit, because anything that disagrees with the recomputation gets clamped or refused server-side.

	**•**	Each roll’s seed also mixes in a drand beacon round (public randomness we don’t control), recorded in the manifest — so we can’t shop for a lucky pre-roll either.

	**•**	When the round resolves, the seals open and verification runs client-side: the player’s phone re-hashes the revealed manifest against the pre-round stamp.  
What this fixes: retroactive dice-fitting, phantom hits, inflated damage — the whole class of “the narrator adjusted reality after seeing what happened.”

What it doesn’t fix, and can’t: the narrator still chooses targets, stakes, and which fights happen at all. Story bias is real and unprovable. We publish the enforcement ledgers and the check-margin histogram (where loaded dice would statistically surface), but I’m under no illusion that’s the same thing.

Worked example with shasum one-liners you can run in a terminal: tabled.gg/fair — the full reference design is at https://tabled.gg/fair/spec.

Happy to go as deep as anyone wants on the constraint machinery — the interesting bugs were all in the seam between “model narrates freely” and “server enforces exactly.”

comments.author: Left-Excitement3829
comments.body: Is this to stop the random Dice not being random ?

replies.author: Fearless_Math_8561
replies.body:
Exactly that. If you ask a language model to “roll a d20,” it doesn’t roll anything, it just writes a number it feels like, and they’re famously biased toward whatever makes the story dramatic. So we took the dice away from the AI completely and a real random roll happens on the server *before* the AI even reads what you typed, gets locked with a cryptographic seal, and the AI has to tell the story around the numbers it was handed. It can’t pick them, and it can’t misreport them either. The game engine recalculates every hit and every point of damage from the sealed rolls, so if the story ever disagreed with the dice, the dice win. After the round, everything unlocks and your phone double-checks the seal itself.

The AI still decides *story* things, like which enemy attacks whom. The dice are honest but the narrator’s taste is still the narrator’s taste.
